contentHtml:
UAE—BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) and Pharmatrade have launched the BD Rowa™ retail pharmacy automation system at Community Health Solutions (CHS) Pharmacy in Wafi Mall, Dubai, marking the technology’s first installation in the UAE.

The deployment aims to improve medication management, strengthen inventory control and increase pharmacy operating efficiency.

Automating medication management

The BD Rowa™ system automates medication storage, retrieval and inventory management, reducing the need for manual handling while improving stock visibility and control.

The technology is designed to help pharmacies manage growing workloads, improve dispensing accuracy and reduce the time pharmacists spend on routine operational tasks.

By streamlining these processes, the system also supports medication safety through improved product traceability, more effective stock rotation and tighter inventory management. This allows pharmacy teams to devote more time to dispensing services and patient care.

The introduction comes as the UAE advances its healthcare transformation agenda, with digital technologies playing an increasingly important role in modernising healthcare delivery.

Pharmacy automation offers an opportunity to address operational pressures associated with growing medicine volumes, inventory complexity and demand for faster, more reliable services.

Expanding pharmacy automation in the region

Ashraf Al Jaabari, Vice President of Pharmacy Automation, Middle East, Türkiye and Africa (META) at BD, said the UAE’s adoption of new technologies was reshaping healthcare delivery, with pharmacy services forming an important part of this transformation.

He noted that the partnership with Pharmatrade would help expand pharmacy automation across the region and support pharmacies in improving services for patients.

Sherif Harydi, General Manager for MENA at BD, said the installation reflected the company’s commitment to supporting the UAE’s healthcare development agenda through technologies that modernise care delivery and improve the patient experience.

Jihad Hussami, Senior Executive Director at Pharmatrade, said the partnership with BD marked an important development for the UAE pharmacy sector.

He noted that introducing the technology at CHS Pharmacy demonstrated how automation could change pharmacy operations and improve customer service.

As medicine demand and pharmacy workloads increase, Hussami highlighted the importance of solutions that improve operational efficiency, inventory visibility and service quality.

Implications for the pharmacy sector

At CHS Wafi Mall Pharmacy, the installation is expected to optimise storage capacity, improve stock visibility and rotation, increase staff productivity and reduce manual handling.

The site will also serve as a reference installation for the UAE market, providing pharmacies with an opportunity to assess how automated medication management can support retail and hospital pharmacy operations.

Its deployment could inform wider adoption of automation technologies as healthcare providers seek to improve inventory management, dispensing processes and operational efficiency.
